c1-12-001.gate_key: adv_agree | C1 | mcq | Which sentence has a mistake? | Each of the rooms have a private bathroom.

key.correct: Each of the rooms have a private bathroom.
wrong: More than one guest has complained about the noise.
Neither of the answers is correct.
One in four adults has never been abroad.

item.why: *each of* + plural noun takes a singular verb: *Each of the rooms has a private bathroom*.
item.why_lv: *each of* + daudzskaitlis prasa darbības vārdu vienskaitlī: *Each of the rooms has a private bathroom.*
item.correct: Each of the rooms have a private bathroom.
wrong: More than one guest has complained about the noise.
Neither of the answers is correct.
One in four adults has never been abroad.

c1-12-002.gate_key: adv_can | C1 | mcq | Choose the correct option: The forecast says snow until April, so this winter ___ unusually long. | may be

item.q: Choose the correct option: The forecast says snow until April, so this winter ___ unusually long.
item.why: A prediction about this particular winter: *may be*. *can be* is for what is generally or sometimes true (*Winters here can be very long*).
item.why_lv: *Prognoze* par šo konkrēto *ziemu*: *may be*. *can be* ir par to, kas mēdz būt vispār (*Winters here can be very long*).

c1-12-003.gate_key: adv_order | C1 | text | Put the focus on *the noise*. Start with *What*: The noise really annoys me. |

accepted: What really annoys me is the noise.

item.q: Put the focus on *the noise*. Start with *What*: The noise really annoys me.
item.why: *What* + verb + *is* + the thing in focus at the end: *What really annoys me is the noise.*
item.why_lv: *What* + darbības vārds + *is* + izceltā lieta beigās: *What really annoys me is the noise.*
answers: What really annoys me is the noise.

c1-12-004.gate_key: adv_order | C1 | mcq | Choose the correct option: Look, there's our bus! Here ___! | it comes

item.q: Choose the correct option: Look, there's our bus! Here ___!
item.why: After *Here*, a noun comes after the verb (*Here comes the bus*), but a pronoun comes before it: *Here it comes!*
item.why_lv: Pēc *Here* lietvārds stāv aiz darbības vārda (*Here comes the bus*), bet vietniekvārds pirms tā: *Here it comes!*

c1-12-005.gate_key: adv_perfect | C1 | gap | I'll text you the moment I ___ my exam results. (get) |

item.q: I'll text you the moment I ___ my exam results. (get)
item.why: *the moment* about the future: present perfect (*the moment I've got my results*) or present simple (*the moment I get my results*), both correct; never *will* or the past.
item.why_lv: *the moment* par nākotni: Present Perfect (*the moment I've got my results*) vai Present Simple (*the moment I get my results*), abi pareizi; nevis *will* vai pagātne.
answer_notes: Also possible: after *the moment* the present simple has the same meaning.
Arī pareizi: aiz *the moment* Present Simple nozīmē to pašu.

c1-12-006.gate_key: adv_perfect | C1 | text | Report what she said with *deny* and *having*. Her words: 'I didn't read the letter.' |

accepted: She denied having read the letter.

item.q: Report what she said with *deny* and *having*. Her words: 'I didn't read the letter.'
item.why: *deny* + *having* + 3rd form for something earlier than the denying: *She denied having read the letter.* (*She denied reading the letter* is natural too.)
item.why_lv: *deny + having* + 3. forma tam, kas notika pirms noliegšanas: *She denied having read the letter.* (*Dabiski* ir arī *She denied reading the letter*.)
answer_notes: Also correct and natural; the task asks for *having*, which shows that the reading came first.
Arī pareizi un dabiski; uzdevums prasa *having*, kas parāda, ka lasīšana bija agrāk.
answers: She denied having read the letter.

c1-12-007.gate_key: adv_prep | C1 | text | Make it more formal. Start with *The colleague with*: The colleague I share an office with is on holiday. |

accepted: The colleague with whom I share an office is on holiday.

item.q: Make it more formal. Start with *The colleague with*: The colleague I share an office with is on holiday.
item.why: Formal: the preposition goes before *whom*: *The colleague with whom I share an office is on holiday.*
item.why_lv: Oficiāli: prievārds stāv pirms *whom*: *The colleague with whom I share an office is on holiday.*
answers: The colleague with whom I share an office is on holiday.

c1-12-008.gate_key: adv_prep | C1 | text | Make it less formal. End the first part with *to*: The person to whom I spoke was very helpful. |

accepted: The person I spoke to was very helpful.
The person who I spoke to was very helpful.
The person that I spoke to was very helpful.

item.q: Make it less formal. End the first part with *to*: The person to whom I spoke was very helpful.
item.why: Everyday style: the preposition goes to the end, and *whom* becomes *who*, *that* or nothing: *The person I spoke to was very helpful.*
item.why_lv: Ikdienas stilā prievārds pāriet uz beigām, un *whom* kļūst par *who, that* vai *izpaliek*: *The person I spoke to was very helpful.*
answers: The person I spoke to was very helpful.
The person who I spoke to was very helpful.
The person that I spoke to was very helpful.

c1-12-009.gate_key: adv_subj | C1 | gap | It's odd that she ___ ___ ___ that at yesterday's meeting. She's usually so polite. |

item.q: It's odd that she ___ ___ ___ that at yesterday's meeting. She's usually so polite.
item.why: After *It's odd / surprising that*, *should* + verb shows surprise; about the past, *should have* + 3rd form: *It's odd that she should have said that.*
item.why_lv: Aiz *It's odd / surprising that should* + darbības vārds izsaka pārsteigumu; par pagātni *should have* + 3. forma: *It's odd that she should have said that.*

c1-12-010.gate_key: adv_subj | C1 | gap | It's odd that she ___ ___ that whenever the topic comes up. She knows it isn't true. |

item.q: It's odd that she ___ ___ that whenever the topic comes up. She knows it isn't true.
item.why: After *It's odd that*, *should* + base form shows surprise about something that keeps happening: *It's odd that she should say that.*
item.why_lv: Aiz *It's odd that should* + pamatforma izsaka pārsteigumu par to, kas atkārtojas: *It's odd that she should say that.*
